title: Thought-Augmented Planning for LLM-Powered Interactive Recommender Agent

problem.claim: Interactive recommender agents need to address diverse and complex user intents, including intuitive, unrefined, or ambiguous requests.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-powered interactive recommender agents have limited planning and generalization capabilities for effectively addressing diverse and complex user intents.

contributions.claim: TAIRA is an LLM-powered multi-agent interactive recommender system that addresses complex user intents through distilled thought patterns.
Thought Pattern Distillation extracts high-level thoughts from agent and human expert experiences to strengthen planning capacity.
TAIRA uses a manager agent to orchestrate recommendation tasks by decomposing user needs and planning subtasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe TAIRA as a novel ThoughtAugmented Interactive Recommender Agent system.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across multiple designed datasets, TAIRA reportedly achieves significantly enhanced performance compared with existing methods.
The authors report that TAIRA solves complex tasks and generalizes effectively to novel tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Interactive recommendation lets users express needs in natural language and receive personalized recommendations.
LLM-powered agents capture real-time needs and improve personalized interactive recommendation experiences.
Existing agents struggle with complex and ambiguous intents because of limited planning and generalization.
TAIRA combines a manager-based multi-agent architecture with Thought Pattern Distillation to improve planning.
Experiments report improved performance, complex-task solving, and generalization to novel tasks.

source_observation.claim: The reported limitation concerns both planning and generalization under complex or ambiguous user intents.

interpretation.claim: Interactive agents may benefit from explicit task decomposition combined with experience-derived planning guidance.

application.claim: For complex interactive recommendation workflows, separate orchestration and planning responsibilities and augment planning with distilled expert or agent experience.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported recommendation tasks and designed datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, sizes, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the Thought Pattern Distillation procedure in implementation detail.
The abstract does not report computational costs, limitations, or failure cases.
